7/23/26, 11:27 AM Print All TIRZ #1 Board Meeting Item # 2.a. Meeting Date: 07/28/2026 Department: Economic Development Key Focus Areas: Economic Development and Revitalization AGENDA CAPTION: Present, discuss, and consider action on the recommendation of the Project and Financing Plan for Tax Increment Reinvestment Zone #1. BACKGROUND: The Board of Directors of the Town of Addison's Tax Increment Reinvestment Zone (TIRZ) #1 is charged with preparing and recommending a Project and Financing Plan for the Zone. This item presents the Final Project and Financing Plan for the Board’s review and recommendation to the City Council, which will consider the Plan for approval during the Regular Meeting. On July 14, 2026, the City Council adopted Ordinance No. 026-028, known as the Creation Ordinance, establishing Reinvestment Zone Number One, Town of Addison (TIRZ #1). This builds on prior Council direction provided over the last two years. At a Tax Increment Financing (TIF) 101 briefing on July 23, 2024, Council directed staff to evaluate a TIRZ for the Transit-Oriented Development. At its November 4, 2025 City Council Work Session Meeting, Council directed preparation of the Project and Financing Plan and gave direction on the Town's stair-step participation rate. Additionally, a TIRZ was recommended specifically for this area by the 2019 Addison Circle Special Area Study. The 2017 Inwood Corridor Enhancement Zone Study identified TIRZs more generally as a tool to support redevelopment and infrastructure reinvestment. Separately, the Town is negotiating an interlocal agreement with Dallas Area Rapid Transit (DART) under which DART would contribute to the TIRZ #1 Fund on terms comparable to a participating unit, anticipated at approximately 60% for a term still under negotiation. This contribution would be made through the interlocal agreement rather than as a Chapter 311 tax increment participation, as DART is not a taxing unit. Upon the Board’s recommendation, the Final Project and Financing Plan will be presented to the City Council for approval. FISCAL IMPACT The Final Project and Financing Plan reflects the Zone as created. The tax increment base is the appraised value of taxable real property within the Zone as of January 1, 2026, estimated at approximately $1.48 billion. The Plan identifies approximately $183.6 million in eligible project costs, allocated across categories eligible under Chapter 311: economic development grants (30%), pedestrian enhancements (18%), parking and transit (15%), street and intersection (15%), open space and public facilities (15%), public utilities (5%), and administrative costs (2%). These figures are estimates and may be revised, with savings in one category applied to another, and individual allocations brought to the TIRZ Board and City Council for consideration. RECOMMENDATION Staff recommends approval. CARES Act Updates
Community Development Block Grant-CV 
Follow-up
and
Emergency Solutions Grant-CV Round 2
Community and Neighborhood Development Committee
June 23, 2020
Discussion Items
1. CARES Act Follow-up Questions
• Job training and retraining resources
• Medical clinics and testing resources
2. Community Development Block Grant – CV
• Options for $400,000 for child care support
• Next steps
3. Emergency Solutions Grant – CV Round 2
• Arlington received $2,977,176 in ESG-CV 2
• Discuss coordinated strategy for use of funds 
1. CARES Act Follow-up Questions 
• Job Training and Retraining Resources
• Medical Clinic Resources
Job Training – COVID-19 Grants & Other Resources
• COVID-19 Dislocated Worker Grant $12 million to Texas Workforce 
Commission (TWC)
• States may sub-grant funds to local boards and/or expend funds through public/private 
agencies
• Allowable activities: disaster relief employment, employment and training services and 
supportive services
• Workforce Solutions for Tarrant County
• Career Training
• Adult Education
• Specialized Programs
• Training and educationalopportunities
• Tarrant County College Opportunity Center, Good Will Industries, Arlington Public 
Library, Small Business Administration and Division for Enterprise Development at UTA
Medical Clinics – CARES Act Funds
• CARES Act Provider Relief Fund providing additional funds to Medicaid 
and CHIP Providers
• Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA) Enhanced Provider Relief 
Fund Portal
• Payment will be at least 2% of reported gross revenue from patient care
• According to the CDC HHS Provider Relief Fund dataset, $40,862,483 has been 
provided to 249 Arlington healthcare providers as of June 17th
• Webcast today June 23 and Thursday June 25 to learn more about the 
application process
• HRSA CARES Act – $1.3 billion
• HRSA Coronavirus Preparedness and Response Supplemental Funding
2. CDBG-CV Status
• Arlington received $2,004,017 in CARES Act CDBG-CV to focus on activities 
that prevent, prepare for, and respond to COVID-19.
• On June 9, the CND Committee discussed the following funding categories for 
CDBG-CV funds:
• Emergency Rental Assistance: $800,000
• Non-Profit COVID-19 Services: $457,661
• Administration/Compliance: $346,356
• To Be Determined $400,000
• Today’s meeting will focus on follow-up recommendations and next steps for 
the use of $400,000
Child Care Needs
• During the declaration of emergency related to COVID-19, many child 
care centers were closed or required to serve only children of 
essential workers
• Child care providers lost significant revenue and many are still closed 
or at reduced capacity
• As businesses open up in Arlington, there is an increased need for 
affordable and available child care slots to help families restore and 
maintain income
• At the last committee meeting, members discussed using available 
CDBG-CV funds to support child care services
Child Care Survey
• Child Care Associates (CCA) has been collecting data from child care providers in Tarrant 
County.  The following is survey data from June 8.
• Of 415 sites reporting, 103 were from Arlington (25%)
• Of 9,879 child care slots, 2,276 were from Arlington (23%)
• In Tarrant County, 67% of child care providers were open and 33% closed due to COVID-19
• In Arlington, 74% of providers were open and 26% were closed, representing about 592 
child care slots closed due to COVID-19
• More centers are opening each week
Child Care 
Provider 
Needs
• Personal protective equipment (PPE)
• Cleaning supplies
• Diapers and formula
• Paid slots for low-income children
• Administrative support for functions such as 
payroll, accounting, training
• General operating expenses for COVID-19 losses
Support for Child Care Providers
• Texas Rising Star (TRS)
• TRS Boost Program
• Licensed Centers
Focus on Quality
Arlington Texas 
Rising Star 
Providers:
4 Stars: 20
3 Stars: 5
2 Stars: 10

TX Rising Star Location Map

Raising the 
Quality Level 
of Providers
• The Boost program provides resources to child care providers 
to help them achieve Texas Rising Star certification.
• Support for providers in the Boost program can be an 
incentive to participate in programs that improve quality 
outcomes for children

Funding Options and Recommendations 
Outcomes will focus on:  1) increased access to quality child care for low -income and 
minority children and families impacted by COVID-19; 2) improved skills of children 
enrolled in quality care; 3) increased household income through improved access to job 
training and job placement.
Coordinate with and fund an umbrella organization with the capacity to administer and 
fund:
Child Care slots in Texas Rising Star 
Centers for low-income and minority 
children
Supplies and resources for Texas Rising 
Star Centers, Boost Centers, and other 
licensed centers
Support for centers to include access to 
training, operating funds, administrative 
support, and quality resources
Next Steps 
• Identify child care organizations with 
capacity to administer CDBG-CV funds and 
offer a range of services to providers and 
families
• Bring back additional details to the Council 
Committee on August 4
• Negotiate a grant agreement to meet child 
care needs in Arlington
• Full Council review on August 18
3. Emergency Solutions Grant-CV Round 2
• Arlington received $2,977,176 in ESG-CV 2
• Funds can be used for:
• Homeless Shelters and Support Services
• Rapid Rehousing for most at risk of COVID
• Targeted Homeless Prevention
• Homeless Outreach
• Homeless Management Information System
• Grant Administration/Compliance
• Needs Assessment and Gaps Analysis Underway
• Coordination across Arlington, Fort Worth, Tarrant County, State of Texas, and Homeless Coalition
• Entities are collaborating to identify gaps and strategies for use of ESG-CV funds
• Staff will bring back more information to the Committee on August 4th
Discussion
Job Training – Resources Available to Residents

evidence.span:
Streets and Transportation Subcommittee
                                2024 Bond Task Force


 Meeting Date: June 13, 2023 Convened: 6:00pm                Adjourned: 7:35pm


 Committee Members Present:                   Committee Members Absent:
 Linda Koop- Chair                            Rudolfo Grvel- District 4
 Beverly Mendoza- District 1                  Jon- Bertrell Killen- District 8
 Patti Simon- District 2                      Marie Appel- District 11
 Portia Greer- District 3
 Grady McGahan- District 5
 Sharon Howard- District 6 (Virtual)
 Jennifer Grantham- District 7
 Courtney Spellicy- District 9
 Susan Morgan- District 10 (Virtual)
 Maura Schreier-Fleming- District 12
 Candice Cook Irvin- District 13 (Virtual)
 Darren Wayne Dattalo- District 14

 Staff Present:
 PBW – Alireza Hatefi                         TRN- Ghassan ‘Gus’ Khankarli
 PBW – Derek White                            TRN- Kimberly Smith
 PBW – Shahad Mohammed
 PBW- Dipendra Timalsina-Sharma


Discussion Items:
The Department of Public Works (PBW) introduced their staff and started the presentation
by defining the Needs Inventory, explaining criteria for projects to be placed on the Needs
Inventory list for each asset managed by Public Works, and listing the project categories
that are on the Needs Inventory. Also, PBW presented the overall City Needs per asset
and their percentages along with a detailed data presentation of the Needs share per
Council District for each asset. Public Works staff continued with defining Citywide
projects and categories that would be considered as “Citywide” by referencing the April
2023 Memo to Mayor and Members of the City Council, “2024 Bond Program Development
– Definition of “Citywide” Projects” . Then, they presented a Data comparison for Alleys on
the Needs Inventory per Council District as well as improved versus unimproved alleys.
Afterwards, they covered the Sidewalk Master Plan focus areas and the top priority
bridges list on the Needs Inventory. Sidewalks and Bridges priority lists were also
provided. In the end, staff presented several budget scenarios with the proposed
 allocations breakdown per each asset. Finally, staff opened the questions and answers
session and answered Subcommittee Members’ questions below.


Questions:
   •   Is the information provided today from the presentation most current?
   •   Is pedestrian fatalities included in the technical ranking criteria for sidewalks?
   •   If the area of concern is not identified on the masterplan as a focus area or high
       priority area what can be done to identify request for consideration?
   •   How can we submit our request for our high priorities for our area?
   •   Do the council members receive a priority list for all the projects first?
   •   How are bike lanes funded and under what department?
   •   What is the time frame for improvements funded through federal funds?
   •   How are thoroughfares classified?
   •   Are traffic lights part of street improvements?
   •   How often is the Needs Inventory List updated/reclassified?
   •   How is funding divided between unimproved and improved alleys?
   •   Why there is a disproportion for alley improvements per district?
   •   How is the funding mechanism per council district to ensure equity based on
       Needs?
   •   How do you know if districts with higher percentage in Needs will also have higher
       number of higher score projects?
   •   Is the bridges maintenance based on safety issue or cosmetics concern?
   •   How are sidewalk projects identified in the arts district?
   •   Will the funding remaining from 2017 Bond Program be reprogramed for 2024
       Bond?
   •   How do you address needs and determine the appropriate funding for the Sidewalk
       Replacement Program?
   •   Is the Senior Sidewalk Replacement assistance advertised?
   •   What is the difference between the Sidewalk Replacement Program and Senior
       Sidewalk Replacement assistance?
   •   What is the eligibility for seniors to be received sidewalk replacement assistance?
   •   What is the contact number for the Sidewalk Replacement Team?
   •   Are sidewalk repairs in parks funded by the Parks and Recreation Department or
       by Public Works?
   •   What is the best way to identify areas of concerns through 311 app?
   •   Are focus areas on the DSWMP improvements repaired by chronological order?
   •   Do the numbers 1-12 indicate the order in which the sidewalks will be addressed?
       (Virtual)
   •   Why the number of Bridges in the previously sent presentation is less than the
       current presentation? (Virtual)
 After the meeting was adjourned, staff stayed to answer questions. The meeting
concluded at 7:35 p.m.
Action Items:
   •   Send out the presentation
   •   City staff to submit the revised excel sheet for alleys to include a tab per council
       district.
   •   Provide response to the questions submitted virtually through WebEx.

evidence.span:
Streets and Transportation Subcommittee
                                 2024 Bond Task Force


 Meeting Date: May 25, 2023      Convened: 6:35pm                Adjourned: 8:00pm


 Committee Members Present:                      Committee Members Absent:
 Linda Koop- Chair                               Patti Simon- District 2
 Beverly Mendoza- District 1                     Rudolfo Grvel- District 4
 Portia Greer- District 3                        Sharon Howard- District 6
 Grady McGahan- District 5
 Jennifer Grantham- District 7
 Jon- Bertrell Killen- District 8
 Courtney Spellicy- District 9
 Susan Morgan- District 10
 Marie Appel- District 11
 Maura Schreier-Fleming- District 12
 Candice Cook Irvin- District 13
 Darren Wayne Dattalo- District 14




 Staff Present:
 TRN – Dr. Ghassan ‘Gus’ Khankarli               PBW – Alireza Hatefi
 TRN – Aurobindo Majumdar                        PBW – Haytham Hassan
 TRN – Kathryn Rush                              PBW – Derek White
 TRN – Kimberly Smith                            PBW – Shahad Mohammed


Discussion Items:
The Department of Public Works introduced their staff and provided an overview of the meeting
topics. They provided background information on both departments’ different and overlapping
projects responsibilities, background information on scoring methodology for the Bond Program
and the 20 points for Equity and Overlays, and a recap from the previous meeting on the
Department of Public Works’ specific responsibilities. Then, they went over Public Works’ project
categories and their definitions with picture examples. Afterwards, they covered the Technical
Criteria for scoring all of Public Works’ project categories and the scoring methodology.


The Department of Transportation continued the presentation by introducing their team and going
over Transportation Plan and Policy Guidance, which included the Connect Dallas Strategic
Mobility Plan. To conclude the presentation portion of the meeting, they covered the
Transportation project categories with example pictures, and their Technical Criteria for scoring
projects.
 At the end of the meeting, both departments went over next steps and suggested adding another
meeting in July to cover all the project categories in the Needs Inventory. They then opened the
Questions and Answers session together and addressed the following questions.
Questions:

   •   How is the Needs Inventory updated?
   •   What is the oldest project in the Needs Inventory list?
   •   For the June 13 meeting, will there be sufficient time to present all projects and have
       questions in an hour and a half meeting?
   •   Are they voting as a group or individually when selecting projects?
   •   Is it possible to have federal funds rather than City?
   •   Is it possible to not fund Partnership Projects?
   •   How does the City determine how many points 311 service requests get to the overlay
       score.
   •   How to add a project as a Residents to the Needs inventory
   •   How to find the maps to be used for the Overlay points?
   •   District 10 would like to know how soon they can have a copy of the last meeting’s
       presentation.
Staff stayed after the meeting was adjourned to answer questions. The meeting concluded at 8:00
p.m.
Action Items:

   •   Have the presentation for the next meeting ready and provide to the Subcommittee 4-5
       days in advance
   •   Confirm if it is allowed by the Bond office and City Attorney to add another meeting in July
   •   Send out the Field Trip details
   •   Send out previous and current meeting presentation slides
   •   Send out links to the Needs Inventory and useful maps
   •   Send out definitions for the Public Works technical criteria factors
   •   Send out information on High Crime Areas.

REGISTRATION GUIDELINES FOR ADDRESSING THE LIBRARY ADVISORY BOARD.
Due to COVID -19 precautions, members of the public will not be able to attend the May 13, 2021 Library 
Advisory Board meeting in person. To accommodate and receive input on agenda items, citizens will be able to  
participate in one of the following ways (NOTE: Other than public hearings, citizens are only able to comment 
one time per agenda item; citizens cannot use both methods to comment on a single agenda item. Public 
comments are not held for work session reports.):
• Virtual White Card – On May 10, the agenda was posted online at www .cityofdenton.com/publicmeetings. 
Once the agenda is posted, a link to the Virtual White Card, an online form, will be made available under the 
main heading on the webpage. Within this form, citizens may indicate support or opposition and submit a brief 
comment about a specific agenda item. Comments may be submitted up until the start of the meeting, at which 
time, the Virtual White Card form will be closed. Similar to when a citizen submits a white card to indicate their 
position on the item, these comment forms will be sent directly to members of the Library Advisory Board and 
recorded by the Secretary
Members review comments received in advance of the meeting and take that public input into consideration 
prior to voting on an agenda item. The Chair will announce the number of Comment Cards submitted in 
support or opposition to an item during the public comment period. Comments will not be read during the 
meeting. The Secretary will reflect the number of comments submitted in favor /opposition to an item, the 
registrant’s name, address, and (summary of) comments within the Minutes of the Meeting, as applicable.
OR
• By phone – Citizens wishing to speak over the phone during this meeting, may call (940) 349-7800 
beginning 30 minutes prior to the meeting start time. Comments by phone will be accepted until the item is 
opened for discussion by the Chair. When the call is initially received, a staff member will receive the caller ’s 
information and either: 1) offer to call the citizen back when it is time for them to speak, or 2) record the 
caller’s information, support or opposition, and comment. If the caller chooses to record their support or 
opposition, rather than speaking during the meeting, the Chair will announce the number of comments 
submitted in support or opposition to the item. If the caller wishes to receive a call back, the voice of each 
caller will be broadcast into the meeting during the public commenting time of their desired agenda item . 
Individuals will be able to comment once per agenda item, no matter the method.

AGENDA
CITY OF DENTON CITY COUNCIL
March 3, 2014
After determining that a quorum is present, the City Council of the City of Denton, Texas will convene in a Joint Meeting with the Library Board on Monday, March 3, 2014 at 12:00 p.m. in the Council Work Session Room at City Hall, 215 E. McKinney Street, Denton, Texas at which the following items will be considered:
Click here for Agenda Backup
1.
Call to order; announce quorum, introductions.
2.
Receive a report, hold a discussion and give staff direction regarding the Denton Public Library Annual Report and Strategic Plan.
3.
Under Section 551.042 of the Texas Open Meetings Act, respond to inquiries from the City Council or the public with specific factual information or recitation of policy, or accept a proposal to place the matter on the agenda for an upcoming meeting  AND  under Section 551.0415 of the Texas Open Meetings Act, provide reports about items of community interest regarding which no action will be taken, to include: expressions of thanks, congratulations, or condolence; information regarding holiday schedules; an honorary or salutary recognition of a public official, public employee, or other citizen; a reminder about an upcoming event organized or sponsored by the governing body; information regarding a social, ceremonial, or community event organized or sponsored by an entity other than the governing body that was attended or is scheduled to be attended by a member of the governing body or an official or employee of the municipality; or an announcement involving an imminent threat to the public health and safety of people in the municipality that has arisen after the posting of the agenda.
Following the completion of the Joint Meeting, the City Council will convene in a Closed Meeting to consider specific items when these items are listed below under the Closed Meeting section of this agenda.  The City Council reserves the right to adjourn into a Closed Meeting on any item on its Open Meeting agenda consistent with Chapter 551 of the Texas Government Code, as amended, or as otherwise allowed by law.
1.
Closed Meeting:
A.
Consultation with Attorneys - Under Texas Government Code Section 551.071.
1.
Consult with and provide direction to City’s attorneys regarding legal issues and strategies associated with Gas Well Ordinance regulation of gas well drilling and production within the City Limits and the extraterritorial jurisdiction, including Constitutional limitations, statutory limitations upon municipal regulatory authority, statutory preemption and/or impacts of federal and state law and regulations, standstill agreements or other cessation regulations and take any appropriate action regarding the above in the meeting of today’s date as it concerns municipal regulatory authority or matters relating to enforcement of the ordinance.
Following the completion of the Closed Meeting, the City Council will convene in Open Session to consider the following item:
1.
Consider adoption of an ordinance of the City of Denton, Texas amending Ordinance Nos. 2013-330 and 2014-040 to extend a "Standstill Agreement" between the City of Denton, Texas and Eagleridge Operating, LLC until midnight on May 6, 2014 with regard to certain disputes and issues over gas drilling in the City to allow the parties an opportunity to engage in global settlement negotiations as it concerns unresolved issues between them; and providing for an effective date.
C E R T I F I C A T E

______________________________
CITY SECRETARY

Council Work Session Room3:00 PMWednesday, October 21, 2020
After determining that a quorum is present, the Animal Shelter Advisory Committee will convene in a regular 
meeting on Wednesday, October 21, 2020, at 3:00 p.m. in the Council Work Session Room at City Hall, 215 
E. McKinney Street, Denton, Texas at which the following items will be considered:
Note:  Chair Diana Leggett, Vice -Chair Ann Sullivan and Members Angie Paben, Charlie Hunter, and Jon 
Birden will be participating in the regular meeting via video teleconference.
1.  ITEMS FOR CONSIDERATION
Consider the approval of the minutes for the July 23, 2020 meeting.ASAC20-006
Exhibit 1 - Draft MinutesAttachments:
Receive a report and hold a discussion regarding:
a. Shelter Statistics
b. Shelter Operations Update
c. Proposed Tethering Ordinance Amendments
d. Proposed Dangerous Dog Amendments
ASAC20-007
Exhibit 1 - Statistics and Operations Update
Exhibit 2 - Tethering Ordinance Amendment
Attachments:
2.  CONCLUDING ITEMS
A.  Under Section 551.042 of the Texas Open Meetings Act, respond to inquiries from the Animal Shelter 
Advisory Committee or the public with specific factual information or recitation of policy, or accept a proposal 
to place the matter on the agenda for an upcoming meeting and under Section 551.0415 of the Texas Open 
Meetings Act, provide reports about items of community interest regarding which no action will be taken, to 
include: expressions of thanks, congratulations, or condolence; information regarding holiday schedules; an 
honorary or salutary recognition of a public official, public employee, or other citizen; a reminder about an 
upcoming event organized or sponsored by the governing body; information regarding a social, ceremonial, or 
community event organized or sponsored by an entity other than the governing body that was attended or is 
scheduled to be attended by a member of the governing body or an official or employee of the municipality; or 
an announcement involving an imminent threat to the public health and safety of people in the municipality that 
has arisen after the posting of the agenda.
CERTIFICATE
I certify that the above notice of meeting was posted on the bulletin board at the City Hall of the City of 
Denton, Texas, on the 16th day of October, 2020 at 8:40 a.m.
____________________________________

family_policy.identity: Use convened body, not venue, topic or common members; numbered boards differ.
family_policy.joint: Same recording may serve every proven participant; separate subscription aggregation from identity.
family_policy.publication: Ordinary public comment does not add Public Info membership; ceremonies are excluded.
family_policy.untracked: An unassigned real body is not automatically a non-meeting. Missing proof permits abstention.
